job.title: Consultant - Business Advisory
job.description:
Consultant – Business Advisory

Join Davidson Strategy & Performance and build your consulting career.


We are looking for a Consultant – Business Advisory to join our growing team and contribute to meaningful consulting engagements across a diverse range of public and private sector clients.

This is an opportunity for an early-career consulting professional who enjoys solving problems, working with data, understanding how organisations operate and turning information into practical insights.

Working alongside experienced Senior Partners, Senior Consultants and project teams, you will gain exposure to a broad range of business advisory engagements while building your consulting capability across analysis, research, stakeholder engagement and client delivery.


About Davidson

Davidson is one of Australia’s leading workplace performance companies. For over 30 years, we have partnered with public and private sector clients to enhance workplace performance.

Davidson Strategy & Performance delivers pragmatic, outcome-focused advice grounded in industry knowledge and consulting expertise. We work alongside clients to achieve measurable and sustainable impact across:

  • Strategy & Operations
  • Transformation Delivery
  • Talent & Leadership Advisory

Our experienced team combines practical insight with proven consulting methodologies to help organisations navigate change, strengthen performance and create sustainable outcomes.

About the Role

As a Consultant – Business Advisory, you will support the delivery of client engagements across strategy, transformation, organisational performance and related advisory services.

You will work closely with experienced consultants to research issues, analyse data, gather stakeholder insights and help develop practical recommendations for clients.

You will take ownership of defined pieces of work, contributing to project deliverables and stakeholder activities while building your confidence and capability as a consultant.

This is a role designed for someone who wants to develop their career in consulting and is looking for the opportunity to learn from experienced practitioners while gaining genuine exposure to client work.

What You'll Be Doing

You will:

  • Support the delivery of consulting engagements across strategy, transformation and business advisory projects.
  • Undertake research, financial analysis, data analysis, benchmarking and desktop analysis.
  • Help identify trends, issues, opportunities and insights from qualitative and quantitative information.
  • Assist with stakeholder interviews, workshops and client meetings.
  • Prepare analysis, reports, presentations and other high-quality client deliverables.
  • Support the development of practical recommendations and implementation-focused outputs.
  • Work collaboratively with Senior Partners, Senior Consultants and project team members.
  • Manage your allocated tasks, priorities and deadlines across multiple pieces of work.
  • Contribute ideas and perspectives to project discussions and problem-solving activities.
  • Support proposals, presentations, research and thought leadership activities.
  • Build your consulting capability through feedback, coaching and hands-on project experience.
  • Contribute to a positive, collaborative team culture and share knowledge as you develop.

What We're Looking For

We are looking for someone who is curious, analytical and motivated to build a career in consulting.

You may come from management consulting, business advisory, professional services, internal consulting, transformation, project delivery, business analysis or a related environment.


You will ideally bring:

  • 1–3 years' professional experience in consulting, business advisory, transformation, project delivery, professional services or a related field.
  • Strong analytical capability and confidence working with data and information.
  • An interest in financial, operational or commercial analysis.
  • Strong research and structured problem-solving skills.
  • The ability to break down complex information and identify key themes or insights.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills.
  • Confidence preparing PowerPoint presentations and written reports.
  • Strong attention to detail and pride in producing high-quality work.
  • The ability to organise your workload, manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.
  • A collaborative approach and willingness to seek feedback and learn from others.
  • Curiosity about how organisations operate, perform and transform.
  • Valid work rights for Australia and can work full time

A relevant tertiary qualification in Business, Commerce, Human Resources, Psychology, Public Policy or a related discipline is preferred.


Experience in any of the following would be advantageous:

  • Strategy or transformation projects
  • Business improvement
  • Organisational performance
  • Workforce or operating model projects
  • Financial or commercial analysis
  • Data analysis or benchmarking
  • Project or programme delivery
  • Change management
  • Workshop or stakeholder engagement

Postgraduate qualifications or relevant consulting, project management or change management certifications are welcomed but not essential.

What You'll Gain

This is an opportunity to develop your consulting career in an environment where you will work directly alongside experienced practitioners and gain exposure to a broad range of client challenges.

You will have the opportunity to:

  • Build your consulting toolkit across strategy, transformation and business advisory.
  • Work directly with experienced Senior Partners and Senior Consultants.
  • Develop your commercial, analytical and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Gain exposure to senior client stakeholders and varied industries.
  • Take increasing ownership of project activities as your capability develops.
  • Receive coaching, feedback and practical development opportunities.
  • Contribute to Davidson's broader intellectual property, research and thought leadership.

Why Join Davidson

At Davidson, we believe when people thrive, organisations thrive.

You will be part of a collaborative, value-driven organisation that puts people at the centre of its success. We offer the opportunity to work with experienced leaders in a lean, agile environment where you can make a genuine contribution.

  • A national brand with strong market presence and long-term client relationships.
  • Flexible hybrid working - 3 days in office.
  • A collaborative culture built around purpose, excellence, care and opportunity.
  • Direct access to senior leaders and decision makers.
  • Learning and development opportunities aligned to your career goals.
  • Recognition programs celebrating individual and team contributions.
  • Team activities including high achievers' lunches, celebration events, values awards and team dinners.

Ready to Build Your Consulting Career?

If you're looking for an opportunity to develop your consulting capability, work on meaningful client engagements and learn from experienced practitioners, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today to join Davidson as our next Consultant – Business Advisory.

job.title: APS6 Senior Procurement Officer

job.title: Senior Estimator – Construction & Fitout
job.description:
Senior Estimator – Construction & Fitout

An established and growing construction and trade services business is looking for an experienced Senior Estimator to strengthen its construction and fitout capability.

This is a newly created role driven by growth. You’ll join two talented developing estimators and become the senior technical presence within the team – remaining hands-on with estimating while providing guidance, structure and mentoring.

The opportunity

This isn’t a role where you’ll step away from estimating to purely manage people. You’ll be actively involved in tenders while helping improve the overall quality and sophistication of the estimating function.

You’ll take responsibility for:

  • Leading and preparing construction and fitout estimates and tenders from initial review through to submission
  • Producing accurate cost plans, take-offs, labour and material build-ups and subcontractor pricing
  • Improving the quality of tender submissions, including methodologies, programmes, qualifications and supporting documentation
  • Reviewing commercial risks, scope gaps, assumptions and margin before submission
  • Providing practical guidance and mentoring to two developing estimators
  • Developing and improving estimating software, systems, templates and cost information
  • Working closely with operations to ensure successful tenders transition effectively into project delivery
  • Building strong relationships with subcontractors, suppliers and key internal stakeholders

About you

You’ll be an experienced estimator who has remained close to the construction and fitout market in recent years and still enjoys being hands-on.

Ideally, you’ll bring:

  • Strong recent estimating experience across commercial construction, fitout or refurbishment projects
  • Confidence managing tenders from initial documentation through to final submission
  • Strong understanding of construction costs, subcontractor packages, programmes and commercial risk
  • Experience producing high-quality tender methodologies and documentation
  • The ability to review and improve estimating processes and systems
  • The capability to mentor less experienced estimators without needing to formally “manage” them
  • A calm, considered and collaborative approach

Why consider this opportunity?

You’ll be joining a business with ambitious growth plans at a point where you can have a genuine impact on how the estimating function develops.

Rather than inheriting a rigid corporate structure, you’ll have the opportunity to bring your experience, improve systems and standards, develop two promising estimators and help shape a function that will support the next stage of the organisation’s growth.

Please submit your current resume to apply in Word document format.

job.title: AO5 Advisor - Real-time Network Management
job.description:
AO5 Advisor - Governance, Process & Training Framework

If you are good at turning complex processes into clear guidance that people can actually use, this role offers the chance to make a practical impact across a large operational environment.

Davidson Executive & Talent is partnering with a Queensland Government department to appoint an AO5 Advisor - Governance, Process & Training Framework (Real-time Network Management). This role will support improvements to the department's incident and disruption management processes. You will review existing practices, strengthen governance, develop clear instructions and create training materials that can be used by teams across Queensland.

You do not need to come from a technical or systems operations background. What matters is your ability to understand a process, identify what needs to improve and translate that into practical documentation, governance and training.


What you'll be doing

You will work with operational teams and stakeholders to improve the way processes are documented, communicated and applied.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • reviewing and updating disruption management governance documentation
  • developing governance documentation for planned events
  • reviewing existing processes and identifying opportunities for improvement
  • developing procedures, work instructions and supporting materials
  • creating practical training content for system users
  • coordinating the rollout of training across the state
  • supporting workflow procedures and maintaining accurate documentation
  • uploading and maintaining relevant materials in SharePoint
  • supporting data requests as required
  • working with internal and external stakeholders to ensure information is clear, accurate and fit for purpose.

Intrastate travel may be required to operational facilities.


What you'll bring

You will be comfortable working through detail while keeping sight of how processes affect the people using them.

We are looking for someone who can bring:

  • experience developing training materials, procedures or work instructions
  • an understanding of governance, risk and compliance
  • strong attention to detail and a focus on data and document quality
  • clear written and verbal communication skills
  • strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities
  • confidence working with a range of stakeholders
  • a practical approach to continuous improvement
  • the ability to learn new processes and systems without needing a technical background.

Experience working in government, regulated or operational environments may be useful, but your ability to develop clear governance, documentation and training will be particularly important.


The engagement

The proposed contract runs from 1 October 2026 to 25 June 2027, with the possibility of extension.

The role is up to 38 hours per week, Monday to Friday, with hours worked between 7 am and 6 pm. No resource is required during the shutdown period from 24 December 2026 to 3 January 2027, or on public holidays during the engagement.

If you enjoy bringing structure to complex processes and creating guidance that helps people work with greater clarity and consistency, we would like to hear from you.



Apply NOW to be considered for this opportunity.

job.title: Manager, Water and Waste
job.description:
Lead essential services. Shape critical infrastructure. Make an impact you can see.

There are leadership roles where you maintain what already exists. Then there are opportunities to shape what comes next.

Davidson Executive & Talent is partnering with Cook Shire Council to appoint its next Manager Water and Waste, leading the essential water, wastewater and waste services that support communities across one of Queensland’s most unique regions.

Based in Cooktown and reporting to the Director Infrastructure, you’ll lead an experienced team of approximately 28 people across water, wastewater, waste and electrical maintenance. You’ll also oversee an operating budget of approximately $9.3 million across these essential services.

Your remit combines technical leadership with asset management, commercial thinking, regulatory compliance and long-term service planning.

The opportunity
This is a role for a leader who wants to build, improve and influence.

There is a significant infrastructure agenda ahead, including new and upgraded water and wastewater infrastructure in Lakeland and Coen, alongside the opportunity to strengthen asset management and shape a practical future waste strategy.

Your early priorities will be clear:

  • Strengthen regulatory and legislative compliance
  • Improve asset management and long-term infrastructure planning
  • Lead, mentor and get the best from an experienced, long-tenured team
  • Build robust business cases that connect infrastructure needs with funding and investment decisions
  • Bring a commercial lens to operational and capital planning
  • Manage and optimise a significant operating budget across water, wastewater and waste services
  • Work confidently with executives, councillors, regulators, contractors and communities

The role spans a large geographic footprint, so visible leadership matters. You’ll spend time with your people, understand the assets firsthand and be comfortable getting out across the region rather than leading solely from behind a desk.

The leader we’re looking for
Your strongest technical grounding will be in water and wastewater. You understand treatment, infrastructure, compliance and the consequences of getting essential services wrong.

You’ll also bring:

  • Leadership experience across water, wastewater and/or waste services
  • Strong asset lifecycle, renewal and capital planning capability
  • Commercial and financial acumen, including responsibility for significant operating budgets and business cases
  • Sound knowledge of relevant regulatory and environmental requirements
  • Experience leading people through change and improving established ways of working
  • The ability to turn complex technical issues into clear recommendations and gain stakeholder support
  • Strong judgement, communication and stakeholder management skills
  • Relevant engineering qualifications or extensive equivalent experience

You don’t necessarily need to come directly from local government. If you bring the technical credibility, commercial judgement and leadership capability, Council can support you in understanding its processes and environment.

Why Cooktown?
Cooktown may not have been where you expected your next career move to take you. That could be exactly what makes this opportunity worth exploring.

You’ll be joining a close-knit organisation with people who care deeply about their community. Council’s Director Infrastructure describes the management team as among the best they have worked with across their career in Australia and internationally, highlighting its integrity, low-ego approach and genuine commitment to community outcomes.

Cooktown offers a very different pace to metropolitan life, without being disconnected from the essentials. The region has schools, health services and airport access, with Cairns approximately a 45-minute flight away. Housing can be challenging, and Council can assist successful candidates in navigating local accommodation options.

We’ll be open about the move, the location and what the role involves. We want you to understand Cooktown properly and decide whether the opportunity is right for you.

Ready for something different?
If you’re an experienced water and wastewater leader looking for greater scope, visible impact and the opportunity to help shape essential infrastructure for the future, we’d like to start a conversation.

You don’t need to have made your mind up about Cooktown before you call.


For a confidential discussion, contact William Stock at Davidson Executive & Talent on william.stock@davidsonwp.com

job.title: Project Manager
job.description:

job.title: Culture and Capability Manager
job.description:
Davidson is proud to partner with Anglican Church Southern Queensland (ACSQ) in the appointment of a newly created Culture & Capability Manager.

ACSQ is one of 23 Dioceses that form the Anglican Church of Australia. Through its network of parishes, schools, education and care services, community services, ministry education and social justice and advocacy, ACSQ plays an important role in communities across Southern Queensland.

Following a recent organisational culture review, ACSQ is investing in its People & Culture capability and creating this role to help translate the findings and commitments from that review into meaningful and sustainable change.

The opportunity

Reporting to the Group Manager, People & Culture, the Culture & Capability Manager will take ownership of developing and delivering ACSQ's culture and capability agenda.

This is a role for someone who enjoys taking an organisation from insight to action.

You will work closely with senior leaders to understand the organisation, its people and its culture, before translating priorities into a practical roadmap that can be delivered and measured.

Your remit will span culture, organisational development, leadership capability, learning and development, employee engagement and change. You will design and facilitate workshops, develop capability initiatives and annual learning programs, strengthen organisational values and support leaders to create a more connected and leader-led culture.

Communication will also be an important part of the role. You will help create greater visibility around the culture and capability agenda, ensuring employees understand what is changing, why it matters and the progress being made.

Working closely with the People Operations Manager, you will help ensure that improvements to culture and capability are supported by strong People & Culture foundations and contemporary ways of working.

What you will bring

We are looking for an experienced Culture, Capability, Organisational Development or senior People & Culture professional who can operate strategically while remaining highly focused on delivery.

You may have developed culture strategies before, but more importantly, you will be able to demonstrate how you have turned those strategies into action and delivered tangible outcomes.

You will ideally bring:

  • Strong experience across organisational development, culture and capability
  • A solid broader Human Resources / People & Culture foundation
  • Experience designing and delivering organisation-wide culture or change initiatives
  • Leadership and manager capability development experience
  • Strong facilitation skills and confidence leading workshops with varied stakeholder groups
  • Experience developing learning, development and capability frameworks
  • The ability to translate employee feedback and organisational insights into practical priorities and actions
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage employees around change
  • Experience partnering with executives and senior leaders and influencing decisions
  • Strong stakeholder management skills and the ability to build credibility quickly
  • The judgement and political awareness to navigate sensitive organisational issues appropriately
  • Resilience, pragmatism and a genuine bias for action
  • The ability to work independently and achieve outcomes within a relatively lean environment
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications or equivalent professional experience

What is important is an ability to work respectfully within the values and ethos of the Anglican Church and to understand the nuances of a complex, purpose-led organisation.

The person

This role will suit someone who is credible, practical and action oriented.

You will need to be comfortable entering an organisation where there is a genuine appetite for change, but also recognise that sustainable culture change takes time.

You will be able to listen carefully, understand different perspectives and build trust, while still maintaining momentum and appropriately challenging the organisation when decisions need to be made.

Above all, ACSQ is looking for someone who can get things done someone who can develop the framework, bring people with them and then ensure the commitments made translate into visible action.


Why join ACSQ?

This is a rare opportunity to step into a newly created position with the ability to genuinely shape the organisation's future culture and capability.

You will have visibility and support from senior leadership and the opportunity to establish a function and framework that has not previously existed in this form.

Success will mean employees can see and feel the progress being made – through stronger leadership, clearer communication, improved capability and a more connected organisational culture.

The role offers $180,000 + super, with a Brisbane CBD location and some flexibility to work from home. Given the stakeholder and relationship-building requirements of the role, there will be an expectation to spend the majority of the initial period in the office.

If you are an experienced culture and capability professional who enjoys moving beyond strategy into delivery and wants the opportunity to make a meaningful organisational impact, we would love to hear from you.

To apply, please submit your CV through Davidson. For a confidential discussion about the opportunity, please contact Jenny Prince, Client Services Director – Jenny.Prince@davidsonwp.com

job.title: Data Engineer
job.description:
About Barwon Water

Davidson has partnered with Barwon Water to appoint experienced Data Engineers to join its Digital Engineering team and help strengthen the organisation’s enterprise data capability required to support one of regional Victoria’s most significant transformation agendas.

Barwon Water delivers water, sewerage and recycled water services to more than 330,000 people across the Geelong region and surrounding communities. Through a major Digital Business Transformation program, the organisation is investing in new technologies, operating models and ways of working that will shape the future of the business and the communities it serves.

About the Role

  • Design, build and operate scalable batch and near-real-time data pipelines, models and reusable data products that support trusted analytics, reporting and approved AI use cases.
  • Build and maintain data solutions across Microsoft Fabric, including Lakehouses, Warehouses, PySpark notebooks and Data Factory pipelines, transforming enterprise data into trusted datasets and semantic models.
  • Engineer data quality into solutions through validation, profiling, reconciliation and monitoring, ensuring issues are identified and managed before they impact downstream users.
  • Apply modern engineering practices including Git-based source control, automated testing, deployment automation, peer review, monitoring, alerting and production support to deliver reliable and maintainable solutions.

About You

  • Strong hands-on data engineering experience across Microsoft Fabric or comparable modern data platforms such as Azure Databricks, Synapse or Snowflake, with experience building layered Lakehouse architectures, data models and pipelines.
  • Strong SQL and working Python skills, with experience ingesting data from SaaS platforms, cloud services and on-premises enterprise systems using secure and supportable integration patterns.
  • Experience building reliable data pipelines with data quality controls, error handling, monitoring and safe rerun processes, along with the ability to troubleshoot and contribute to root cause analysis in production.
  • A strong technical mindset combined with commercial awareness and a consulting approach, with the ability to explain technical trade-offs to business stakeholders, collaborate with engineers and work effectively within Agile delivery teams.

The Benefits

This is a unique opportunity to contribute to Barwon Water’s growing enterprise data capability during a significant digital transformation. You’ll design scalable data pipelines, models and products that enable trusted analytics, reporting and AI outcomes, while working alongside a collaborative Digital Engineering team committed to innovation and continuous improvement.

Based in Geelong, this permanent full-time role offers a hybrid working model with three days per week in the office, providing flexibility while supporting close collaboration with stakeholders and delivery teams.


Please submit your current resume to apply. If you'd like a confidential discussion about the role, please contact Adnan​ Haidermota on adnan.haidermota@davidsonwp.com, quoting reference JN -092026-44228. To learn more about Davidson, visit davidsonwp.com.

job.title: Senior Program Manager – Projects & PMO
job.description:
Senior Program Manager – Projects & PMO

Davidson is partnering with a growing Australian organisation operating across resource recovery, telecommunications, infrastructure and Defence-related environments to appoint a Senior Program Manager – Projects & PMO.

Reporting to the General Manager, you will lead the national delivery and governance of a diverse project portfolio while developing the organisation’s PMO capability.

This is a senior, hands-on project leadership role focused on creating consistency, strengthening governance and ensuring projects are delivered safely, commercially and in line with contractual, regulatory and customer requirements.

The opportunity

You will take ownership of project performance across a national portfolio, with responsibility for:

  • Providing national oversight across Resource Recovery, telecommunications, infrastructure and Defence-related projects
  • Establishing and developing PMO governance, reporting, systems, templates and delivery standards
  • Leading, coaching and supporting Project Managers and project teams
  • Directly managing high-value, complex or strategically significant projects
  • Monitoring project budgets, forecasts, margins, variations and financial performance
  • Maintaining strong risk, issue, change and escalation processes
  • Ensuring Defence-related projects meet relevant security, contractual, HSEQ and compliance requirements
  • Building strong relationships with clients, executives, operational leaders, contractors and external stakeholders
  • Coordinating project resourcing and workforce capability across multiple locations
  • Driving continuous improvement across project delivery, reporting, governance and operational performance

About you

You will bring significant project management experience delivering complex, multi-site or national projects.

Your background could come from telecommunications, infrastructure, Defence, resource recovery or another complex field-based project environment.

The priority is finding an accomplished project leader with strong capability across:

  • Project governance – risk management, change control, reporting and delivery assurance
  • Commercial performance – budgeting, forecasting, cost control, variations and margin management
  • PMO development – establishing or improving project systems, standards and governance frameworks
  • Leadership – coaching Project Managers, setting clear expectations and building accountability
  • Stakeholder management – confidently engaging with senior executives, clients, contractors and operational teams
  • Compliance – strong understanding of WHS/HSEQ, contractor management and operational requirements

You will also be comfortable managing multiple concurrent projects and competing priorities across different locations, with strong digital literacy across Microsoft Office/Excel and operational or compliance platforms.

The ability to meet any relevant security clearance or Defence-related requirements will also be important.

Leadership with purpose

The organisation combines strong commercial performance with a clear social purpose, creating meaningful employment and development opportunities for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people.

You will bring a leadership style that balances commercial accountability, strong governance and delivery discipline with coaching, inclusion and people development.

Experience working with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people would be valued but is not essential. Alignment with the organisation’s purpose and a willingness to undertake cultural competency training are important.

The opportunity to grow

This role offers the opportunity to shape how projects are delivered nationally, strengthen PMO capability and establish the systems and governance needed to support continued growth.

It could suit an established senior project leader looking for broader portfolio responsibility, or an experienced Program or Project Manager ready to step into a role with greater national leadership and strategic influence.

You will have the opportunity to lead complex and strategically important projects while helping build a more consistent, scalable and commercially disciplined project delivery function.

job.title: National Operations Manager - Resource Recovery
job.description:
Melbourne preferred | Brisbane considered | National remit

Lead national operations. Build consistency. Unlock value from every asset.

Davidson is partnering with a growing Australian organisation operating across resource recovery, recycling and secure asset processing to appoint a National Operations Manager – Resource Recovery.

Reporting to the General Manager and leading approximately 3–4 Site Managers, you will oversee a growing network of processing facilities across Australia.

This is a hands-on leadership role focused on making the national operation work efficiently, consistently and commercially – ensuring valuable assets and recovered materials are accurately tracked, effectively processed and moved through the right channels.

The opportunity

You will take ownership of operational performance across multiple sites, with responsibility for:

  • Leading and developing Site Managers across the national network
  • Establishing consistent operational processes, controls and performance standards
  • Managing the receipt, tracking, processing, storage and movement of assets and recovered materials
  • Maintaining strong inventory reconciliation, asset tracking and chain-of-custody controls
  • Overseeing logistics and material movements between customers, facilities and downstream processors
  • Driving productivity, labour efficiency, safety, cost and margin performance
  • Maximising the recoverable value of processed materials and commodities
  • Monitoring processing volumes, inventory movements and operational KPIs
  • Supporting the establishment and mobilisation of new sites as the network expands
  • Driving continuous improvement across systems, processes and operating models
  • Maintaining strong safety, environmental and regulatory standards

About you

Your background could come from e-waste, metals recycling, resource recovery, secure asset recovery, reverse logistics, waste management, industrial processing, warehousing or logistics.

Direct recycling experience would be advantageous, but the priority is finding an accomplished operational leader with strong capability across:

  • Logistics – transport, material movements, warehousing, scheduling and multi-site coordination
  • Inventory control – reconciliation, stocktakes, shrinkage, chain of custody, asset tracking and audit
  • Operations leadership – leading multiple sites and developing operational managers
  • Commercial performance – improving productivity, labour utilisation, costs and margins
  • Systems and process improvement – experience with ERP, WMS, inventory or production systems

Exposure to commodity pricing, recovered-material sales or downstream processors would be beneficial but isn't essential.

Leadership with purpose

The organisation combines commercial and environmental performance with a strong social purpose, creating meaningful employment and development opportunities for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people.

You will bring a leadership style that combines clear commercial accountability with coaching, inclusion and people development.

Experience working with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people would be valued but isn't essential. Alignment with the organisation's purpose and a willingness to undertake cultural competency training are important.

The opportunity to grow

This could suit an established national leader or an ambitious Regional or State Operations Manager ready to step into their first national role.

You will have the opportunity to shape a growing national operation, develop its people and establish the systems and processes required to support its next phase of growth.

Please submit your current resume to apply. To learn more about Davidson, visit davidsonwp.com

job.title: Temp Administration Assistant | Immediate Start
job.description:

job.title: People Operations Manager
job.description:
Davidson is proud to partner with Anglican Church Southern Queensland (ACSQ) in the appointment of a newly created People Operations Manager.

ACSQ is one of 23 Dioceses that form the Anglican Church of Australia. Through its network of parishes, schools, education and care services, community services, ministry education and social justice and advocacy, ACSQ plays an important role in communities across Southern Queensland.

Following a recent review of the People & Culture function, ACSQ is investing in its capability and creating this role to provide experienced operational leadership across People & Culture.

The opportunity

Reporting to the Group Manager, People & Culture, the People Operations Manager will take ownership of day-to-day People & Culture operations, providing practical and trusted advice to leaders and managers while strengthening the processes, systems and governance that support the employee lifecycle.

This is a hands-on senior HR role. You will work across a diverse stakeholder environment, partnering with senior leaders, managers, clergy and employees to navigate people matters, build manager capability and create a more consistent and contemporary People & Culture service.

A key focus will be supporting a shift towards a leader-led, People & Culture-enabled model building the confidence and capability of managers to take greater ownership of their people, while ensuring they have the right frameworks, advice and support around them.

You will also have the opportunity to identify what can be done differently and better. From improving workflows and reducing manual processes through to strengthening governance, policies, employee records and service delivery, you will play an important role in building the foundations for the future People & Culture function.

What you will bring

We are looking for an experienced People & Culture professional who has operated at this level before and understands what good looks like.

You will bring strong generalist HR capability and demonstrated experience across employee and workplace relations, organisational change, performance, manager coaching and the broader employee lifecycle.

Importantly, you will be someone who can build trusted relationships while still being prepared to provide clear advice and appropriately challenge established ways of working.

You will ideally demonstrate:

  • Significant senior generalist HR experience within a complex organisation
  • Strong employee and workplace relations capability, including the management of complex and sensitive matters
  • Sound knowledge of the Fair Work Act, modern awards and contemporary employment practices
  • Experience improving HR processes, systems, governance and ways of working
  • The ability to coach and influence leaders while strengthening manager accountability
  • Strong stakeholder engagement skills across a diverse organisation
  • Experience working through organisational change or transformation
  • A practical, solutions-focused approach and the ability to turn ideas into action
  • Strong judgement, resilience and the ability to navigate complexity and competing priorities
  • A relevant tertiary qualification in Human Resources, Industrial Relations, Business or a related discipline is desirable

What is important is an ability to work respectfully within the values and ethos of the Anglican Church and an appreciation of the unique environment in which ACSQ operates.

Why join ACSQ?

This is an opportunity to join the organisation at an important point in the evolution of its People & Culture function.

You will work closely with an experienced leadership team, have genuine scope to influence how People & Culture services are delivered and help establish stronger foundations that will support the organisation for years to come.

The role offers $180,000 + super, with a Brisbane CBD location and some flexibility to work from home. Given the relationship-focused nature of the position, there will be an expectation to spend the majority of the initial period in the office and engaging with stakeholders across the Diocese.

If you are an experienced People & Culture leader who enjoys getting close to the business, improving how things work and building trusted relationships, we would love to hear from you.



To apply, please submit your CV through Davidson. For a confidential discussion about the opportunity, please contact Jenny Prince, Client Services Director – Jenny.Prince@davidsonwp.com

job.title: Account Manager - Emerging Accounts
job.description:
About Davidson

Davidson brings together expertise across people, strategy, and technology to help organisations perform at their best. Founded in 1991, we listen closely, understand the challenge and apply practical, experience-led thinking helping organisations move forward with confidence. Our focus is on bringing clarity to complexity and supporting stronger, more resilient futures.

Within Davidson Technology Consulting, we partner with organisations to shape, deliver, and assure technology change, reducing risk and building capability at every scale.

About the Role

Davidson Technology Consulting is growing, and we’re looking for an Account Manager - Emerging Accounts to play a key role in what comes next. You’ll build on Davidson’s existing relationships to expand our Technology Consulting presence across our client network and develop selected new accounts.

You’ll open broader technology conversations, build connections with senior decision makers and identify where our capability can address their needs. Working with Senior Partners and delivery teams, you’ll turn opportunities into stronger client partnerships and sustainable commercial growth.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Grow emerging Technology Consulting accounts across Davidson’s client network, expanding relationships and identifying new areas of opportunity.
  • Open new doors within existing clients, building relationships with senior technology, digital and business decision makers.
  • Create, convert, and grow opportunities to advise, augment capability, or deliver technology outcomes.
  • Develop account growth plans identifying priority stakeholders, opportunities, and clear actions to increase our presence.
  • Build and convert a strong pipeline against commercial targets, with disciplined forecasting, and clear next steps.
  • Turn client and market insight into growth, bringing Davidson relationships and expertise together to develop commercially sound opportunities in priority markets.

What We're Looking For

You’ll have experience growing accounts within consulting, professional services or solution sales. You’ll bring:

  • A track record of growing accounts, creating opportunities, and delivering revenue outcomes.
  • Strong business development capability, with the ability to open new relationships and expand existing ones.
  • Confidence engaging senior and executive stakeholders and turning conversations into opportunities.
  • Commercial judgement and negotiation skills to progress and convert opportunities.
  • An understanding of technology change and how to connect client challenges with relevant solutions.
  • Financial services or complex enterprise experience and established industry networks would be valuable.

job.title: APS6 Senior Performance and Evaluation Officer

job.title: Training Lead - SAP
job.description:
JOB TITLE: Training Lead
JOB LOCATION: Brisbane, QLD
JOB DURATION: 12 – months contract (potential extension or conversion)

Project Context

The public sector client is undertaking a major ERP transformation, migrating a customised SAP ECC6 environment to SAP S/4HANA Private Cloud. The program follows SAP Activate methodology, delivered across multiple horizons and waves, and spans core functions including Finance, Asset Management, Maintenance, Procurement, Payroll and more. Alongside the technical migration, the organisation is using the transformation to rationalise enterprise structures and move toward a "clean core" SAP model. Capgemini is engaged as the Business Transformation/Solution Adoption Partner, supporting the design, build and adoption of the new solution across the organisation.

Role Purpose

The Training Lead is accountable for the successful delivery of the Learning & Capability workstream within Solution Adoption, ensuring the workforce is trained, capable and ready to operate SAP S/4HANA and the associated business process changes. The role leads training strategy, learning needs analysis, curriculum design, content development, delivery and capability uplift throughout the SAP Activate lifecycle, working closely with the Change Lead to ensure learning and change activities are fully integrated.

Key Responsibilities:

Training Leadership & Delivery

  • Lead the end-to-end delivery of the Learning & Capability workstream across all horizons and waves.
  • Develop and execute the Training Strategy, Training Plan and supporting learning materials.
  • Ensure training activities are integrated with solution design, testing, deployment and transition to BAU.

Learning Needs Analysis & Curriculum Design

  • Lead Learning Needs Analysis in parallel with Fit-to-Standard workshops across impacted business functions.
  • Design persona-based, role-specific learning pathways aligned to new SAP S/4HANA processes, responsibilities and system interactions, covering distinct workforce segments such as leadership and executives, people leaders, operational leaders, enabling function users, frontline/technical personnel, administration users and light users.
  • Prioritise and sequence learning content against confirmed business need, addressing both new functionality and refresher training for existing processes requiring capability uplift, rather than developing content generically.
  • Translate Change Impact Assessment outputs and solution design decisions into targeted learning interventions.

Training Content Development & Delivery

  • Lead the development of training materials, facilitator guides, digital learning assets, simulations, job aids and evaluation tools, developed through SAP WalkMe as the primary learning content platform.
  • Design and deliver end-user training and Train-the-Trainer activities during Deploy, using blended modalities suited to a distributed, shift-based and operational workforce.
  • Coordinate training environments, test scripts and scenario-based exercises with functional and technical SAP teams to ensure content reflects the configured solution.

Train-the-Trainer & Capability Uplift

  • Establish and lead the Super User and Trainer network, providing advanced system knowledge and facilitation skills to support peer coaching and local adoption reinforcement.
  • Build sustainable internal capability and support capacity during deployment and beyond go-live, in collaboration with the Change Management team.
  • Deliver refresher training and post-go-live capability reinforcement during Run/Hypercare, supporting transition to business-as-usual ownership.

Governance, RAID & Reporting

  • Own training-related RAID items alongside the project analyst and Business Readiness & Adoption Analyst, including identification, management and escalation of training risks, issues, assumptions and dependencies.
  • Report training completion and competency rates through LMS reporting, attendance records, assessment results, knowledge checks and learner evaluations, feeding into overall business readiness and go-live decision-making.
  • Maintain the Training Needs Analysis and role-based Learning Pathway templates and other governance artefacts, and support training-related governance forums.

Digital Enablement & Insights

  • Oversee the deployment and use of SAP WalkMe, and any complementary digital adoption tooling, to support training delivery and adoption measurement.
  • Leverage training completion data and analytics to identify remaining capability gaps, engagement trends and readiness risks, feeding program-level readiness and adoption dashboards.
  • Provide evidence-based recommendations on training effectiveness and capability uplift to program leadership.

Key Outcomes

  • A workforce trained and capable of operating SAP S/4HANA and new business processes at go-live, with refresher capability uplifted on existing processes.
  • Persona-based training pathway coverage across all impacted functions, waves and workforce segments, including frontline and operational users.
  • Training completion and competency rates tracked and reported against agreed go-live thresholds.
  • Effective integration of training with change, communications and readiness activities across the SAP Activate lifecycle.
  • Sustainable internal capability through Train-the-Trainer and Super User networks.
  • Successful transition to business-as-usual operations and long-term capability ownership.

Experience & Capability

  • Extensive experience leading training or learning workstreams for large-scale ERP and SAP transformations; SAP S/4HANA experience is highly regarded.
  • Demonstrated expertise in Learning Needs Analysis, persona-based curriculum design and training delivery across large, complex, multi-site organisations, including frontline/operational workforces.
  • Hands-on experience developing and governing learning content in SAP WalkMe, and working knowledge of Learning Management Systems for completion tracking and reporting.
  • Experience designing and leading Train-the-Trainer and Super User enablement programs.
  • Strong facilitation, workshop leadership and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Experience working within multi-vendor environments in collaboration with System Integrators, PMOs and business stakeholders.
  • Ability to lead and develop a small training analyst team, and to work collaboratively with the Change Lead to ensure integrated adoption outcomes.



Please submit your current resume to apply. If you'd like a confidential discussion about the role, please contact Bidisha Swayamprava on Bidisha.Swayamprava@davidsonwp.com, quoting reference JN -092026-44340. To learn more about Davidson, visit davidsonwp.com.

job.title: Senior Systems Engineer
job.description:
About the Company

Iberdrola Australia is leading Australia’s transition to a clean energy future. With over 170 years history, the Iberdrola Group today is a global energy leader. Their expertise includes renewable energy, networks, smart grids, large-scale energy storage, energy innovation and digitisation, and advanced customer products.

Their generation portfolio is more than 95% renewable and includes 9 wind farms, 3 solar farms, 2 grid scale batteries and 2 fast-start peakers and continuing to evolve, investing in new capabilities in networks and offshore wind. Iberdrola’s financial strength, supply chain access and history of award-winning expertise, will make Iberdrola a certain partner to accelerate Australia’s Net Zero emissions future.

Iberdrola is now recruiting for a Senior Systems Engineer to work on the new VNI West project based in the Melbourne CBD office.

This is an opportunity to shape your career with one of the genuine global energy leaders within Australia.

About the Role

The Senior Systems Engineer (Systems Engineering and Assurance) will implement and maintain the project Systems Engineering framework, ensuring that stakeholder, regulatory, contractual and technical requirements are captured, managed, allocated, verified and validated throughout the project lifecycle.

The role provides leadership across requirements management, assurance, verification and validation, interface management and systems integration. It ensures alignment with the Systems Engineering Management Plan (SEMP), Systems Engineering Management Framework (SEMF), project governance requirements and applicable international Systems Engineering standards.

The position acts as custodian of requirements traceability and assurance evidence within the Requirements Management System, preferably Relatics, supporting design development, delivery, testing, commissioning and handover.

Some specific responsibilities include:

· Lead the implementation and application of Systems Engineering processes in accordance with ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288 and the project Systems Engineering Management Plan (SEMP).

· Establish, manage and maintain project requirements, including baselines, allocation, traceability, configuration control and change management within Relatics or the approved Requirements Management System.

· Facilitate requirements elicitation, analysis and stakeholder engagement activities to ensure requirements are clear, measurable, verifiable and aligned with project objectives.

· Develop and maintain end-to-end requirements traceability between stakeholder needs, design deliverables, verification activities, assurance evidence and project outcomes.

· Coordinate Contractors, Engineering Designers and Owner’s Engineers to ensure consistent application of Systems Engineering and Systems Assurance approaches across the supply chain.

· Support the development and maintenance of system architectures, system breakdown structures, operational concepts, interfaces and other Systems Engineering artefacts.

· Implement and support Systems Assurance activities, including assurance reviews, governance forums, compliance assessments and stage gate approvals.

· Develop and coordinate verification and validation strategies, plans, matrices and activities to demonstrate compliance with project requirements and operational needs.

· Identify, manage and coordinate system interfaces across project disciplines, contractors, stakeholders, regulators and external parties, ensuring interface risks and actions are effectively managed.

· Administer and optimise Relatics, including workflow configuration, reporting, dashboards, data governance, user support and assurance performance metrics.

· Deliver Relatics training and Relatics configuration development for wider Project Management.

· Assess and manage Systems Engineering, assurance, interface and configuration risks arising from design, requirements and project changes, ensuring impacts are understood and controlled.


About You

To be successful in this role you will have tertiary electrical engineering qualifications and strong experience in a similar role within energy or renewables (preferred) or other large, complex capital infrastructure (rail, defence, utilities). Training and certification with INCOSE will be well regarded.

Your excellent interpersonal skills allow you to build effective working relationships with colleagues and stakeholders, resulting in exceptional performance.

You will be able to work in a very hands-on, flexible and practical manner while thinking strategically, and you will be comfortable and able to travel interstate to both office and site locations when required.

The Benefits

This is an exceptional career opportunity to join a world leader in renewable energy and work on a nationally significant transmission line project.

You’ll lead a small team and work closely with program and corporate stakeholders to improve how information is collected, managed, analysed and communicated. The focus is practical. Build better reporting products. Improve systems and processes. Turn diverse data into useful insights. You’ll also have the opportunity to shape reporting solutions and dashboards, including using tools such as Power BI or similar platforms.


What you’ll be doing

  • identifying trends, risks and opportunities within program information

  • leading improvements to reporting systems, processes and supporting guidance
  • developing training resources that help teams use reporting and data systems effectively
  • working with business and technical stakeholders to turn their needs into practical solutions
  • providing advice on reporting processes, performance information and data management
  • producing clear reports, briefs and information products for senior executive audiences.

What will help you succeed

You’ll be comfortable working with both people and data.

You can move from understanding a business problem to analysing the information, developing a practical reporting solution and explaining the result clearly to stakeholders. We’re particularly interested in experience across program management, governance, reporting, performance monitoring or business improvement.

You’ll also bring:

  • experience leading or supervising a small team
  • strong analytical and conceptual thinking
  • experience sourcing and interpreting information from diverse data sources
  • capability developing dashboards, visualisations or fit-for-purpose reporting products
  • experience with Power BI or similar reporting and visualisation platforms
  • strong stakeholder engagement skills across business and technical teams

job.title: Sleep Expert & Store Manager
job.description:
The best salespeople don't think of themselves as salespeople. They think of themselves as experts who are here to help.

There are few things more important to someone's wellbeing than sleep. At Sleepy's, our Store Managers and teams take the time to understand what's getting in the way of a better night's sleep and help customers find the right solution.

It's why customers choose us - not because we discount harder, but because our advice is genuine.

Davidson is proudly partnering with Sleepy's to find our next Sleep Expert & Store Manager.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You'll be on the floor selling alongside your team, coaching them to improve and taking ownership of your store's people, culture and commercial performance.

Who this is right for
You'll probably be someone who:

  1. Genuinely loves selling and still wants to be on the floor
  2. Gets energy from coaching people and watching them improve
  3. Loves becoming an expert so you can genuinely help customers
  4. Enjoys the commercial side of running a business
  5. Is always looking for a better way to do things
  6. Wants to lead, not simply manage

Maybe you're already doing more than your job title suggests

If your current leader sees you as simply a store location and a set of numbers but your team knows how much you give to make that store successful, then maybe we should chat?

You're the person coaching them, keeping everyone motivated, solving problems and you still love customer interactions - in fact you’re the best salesperson in the team.

If that sounds familiar, we'd like to hear from you.

At Sleepy's, we want our Store Managers to feel as valued as the customers and teams they look after.

If you spend every day trying to make a difference to other people's lives, we'd like the opportunity to make a difference to yours.

You don't need to come from bedding. Furniture, jewellery, automotive, real estate, wellness, premium retail and more - if customers need to trust you before making an important decision, you'll understand what makes this role different.

We can teach you mattresses. We can't teach curiosity, care and the drive to be excellent.

If that sounds like you, we'd love to hear from you.

job.title: Business/Data Analyst
job.description:
About the Company

Our client is a reputable government organisation.

About the Role

Seeking an experienced Business Analyst / Data Analyst to support a transformation portfolio by consolidating multiple source registers into a single, validated and traceable dataset.

ou will work across a range of portfolio and project management artefacts to create a consistent and reliable view of the organisation’s active initiatives.

The successful candidate will be highly analytical, detail-oriented and comfortable working with complex Excel-based registers and inconsistent source data. You will be expected to identify, document and escalate discrepancies for management validation, ensuring that data conflicts are clearly recorded rather than hidden or independently resolved.

Key responsibilities

  • Develop a master initiative crosswalk reconciling names and identifiers across multiple source registers.
  • Bring together schedule, risk, issue, benefits, status and forecast data under common initiative identifiers.
  • Reconcile the initiative population against an agreed inclusion rule and document any exceptions.
  • Populate initiative baseline templates for all active initiatives, including:
    • Baseline dates
    • Dependencies
    • Resource requirements
    • Key delivery information
  • Validate and relink schedule dependencies, including predecessor and successor relationships.
  • Review risk and issue registers for completeness, including ownership, review dates and status.
  • Assess risk and issue information against the organisation’s risk framework and RAID conventions.
  • Reconcile the financial reporting bases currently in use and document the basis supporting each reported figure.
  • Review status and health indicators to ensure they accurately reflect underlying delivery performance.
  • Identify and log data conflicts between source registers for management review.
  • Maintain a data quality tracker documenting fields, sources, issues and remediation status.
  • Prepare a concise handover briefing outlining residual gaps, assumptions and outstanding matters.

Key deliverables:

  • Master initiative crosswalk.
  • Individual-level initiative baseline template for all active initiatives.
  • Re-linked master schedule with dependency integrity checked.
  • Data quality tracker and reconciliation log.
  • Handover briefing note summarising residual gaps and assumptions.

About You

  • Demonstrated experience integrating and reconciling data from multiple, inconsistent source systems.
  • Strong Excel skills, including formulas, pivot tables and data validation.
  • Experience using Power Query, or an equivalent tool, to merge and manage large datasets.
  • Working knowledge of project and portfolio management artefacts, including schedules, RAID logs, benefits registers and baselines.
  • Strong attention to detail and a clear focus on data quality, consistency and traceability.
  • The ability to identify and document discrepancies without concealing or independently resolving them.
  • Strong written communication skills, particularly when documenting assumptions, gaps and reconciliation logic.
  • The ability to manage commercially sensitive portfolio information with discretion.

The Benefits

  • Competitive day rates
  • Initial contract till end of December 2026 with view to extend
  • Hybrid

job.title: A07 Health and Wellbeing Principal Advisor
job.description:
About the Company

Our client is a large and complex organisation delivering civil construction and maintenance services across Queensland. With approximately 1,300 employees, supported by significant labour hire and subcontractor workforces, the organisation operates across a diverse range of environments throughout the state.

With a strong focus on worker health and safety, the organisation is continuing to strengthen its approach to health, wellbeing and workplace risk management.


About the Role

This is an opportunity for an experienced health and wellbeing professional to lead and continuously improve enterprise-wide programs that protect worker health and support a safe, healthy and productive workforce.

This is a senior specialist technical and advisory position with no direct reports. Success will be driven by your subject matter expertise, professional judgement, stakeholder engagement and ability to influence outcomes across the organisation.

Working closely with operational leaders, health and safety professionals, occupational hygiene specialists and external service providers, you will provide specialist leadership and advice across worker health, fitness for work, psychosocial wellbeing and hazardous exposures.

  • Leading health monitoring and health surveillance programs, including governance, implementation, oversight and contractor management
  • Supporting fitness for work programs encompassing fatigue, drug and alcohol management and related assurance activities
  • Leading psychosocial risk management and worker wellbeing initiatives
  • Managing health risks associated with hazardous exposures including lead, respirable crystalline silica, asbestos, noise and chemicals
  • Supporting exposure monitoring programs and associated health-related training
  • Developing and reviewing policies, standards, procedures, guidance materials and governance frameworks
  • Identifying and implementing practical, enterprise-wide solutions to health and wellbeing challenges
  • Providing trusted specialist advice to operational and corporate stakeholders.


About You

You are an experienced health and wellbeing professional who can operate independently, navigate complex issues and translate technical requirements into practical operational outcomes.

You will bring strong professional judgement and the confidence to influence stakeholders without direct authority. Comfortable taking ownership of complex challenges, you can work through technical, operational and stakeholder considerations to deliver effective solutions with minimal supervision.

  • More than five years’ experience across health, occupational hygiene, workplace wellbeing, health and safety or a closely related discipline
  • Demonstrated experience managing legislated health monitoring and health surveillance programs
  • Strong experience implementing fitness for work programs, including fatigue and drug and alcohol management
  • Experience leading psychosocial risk management and workplace wellbeing initiatives
  • Experience developing enterprise-level frameworks, systems, standards, procedures and improvement programs
  • Experience managing health risks associated with hazardous substances and exposures
  • Experience within civil construction, construction, transport, infrastructure, utilities, resources, rail or another comparable high-risk industry
  • The ability to build strong relationships and translate specialist technical requirements into practical business outcomes.


The Benefits

This is an opportunity to step into a senior specialist position offering broad organisational influence and genuine enterprise-wide scope.

Rather than leading through people management, you will lead through expertise, influence and trusted advice. You will have the autonomy to take complex programs from concept through to implementation and play an important role in strengthening worker health and wellbeing outcomes.

You will also have access to occupational hygiene and specialist technical support when required, while taking ownership of governance, programs and practical improvement initiatives across the organisation.

For an experienced practitioner who enjoys solving complex problems, influencing organisational change and delivering meaningful worker health outcomes, this is an opportunity to make an impact across a substantial and diverse operational workforce.

job.title: Market Analyst
job.description:
Davidson is the proud recruitment partner of SEC Victoria as they accelerate Victoria’s renewable energy transition.

Do work that makes a difference

SEC is building an enterprising and dynamic team to accelerate Victoria’s transition to renewables and help achieve Victoria’s renewable energy target of 95% by 2035. We are working together for renewable, affordable, reliable energy for all Victorians.

Your role
As a Market Analyst in the Energy Markets Analytics team, you will deliver insights that inform critical long-term decisions across the organisation. With PLEXOS modelling at the core of the role, you will analyse Australian energy market trends, interpret complex modelling outputs, and provide strategic recommendations to support key business initiatives. You will also contribute to the development of analytical tools and systems that drive data-informed decision-making.

You will bring strong hands-on PLEXOS experience, ideally in short-term price forecasting, with the ability to translate modelling outcomes into actionable insights. Supported by programming skills in Python, R, or SQL, and proficiency in Excel, Power BI, or Tableau, you will combine technical expertise with strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills to deliver value in a fast-paced and collaborative environment.

This role can be based in either our Melbourne CBD office or our regional office located in Morwell.

What you will do:
Core accountabilities include:

  • Modelling & forecasting: Enhance SEC’s market modelling capabilities, including short-term probabilistic forecasts, long-term capacity expansion, and dispatch optimisation models. Improve integration, quality, and usability of outputs to support strategic decision-making.
  • Scenario analysis: Contribute to developing energy transition scenarios by applying market expertise and judgement, and support documentation of assumptions and scenarios for stakeholder and Board endorsement.
  • Project due diligence: Partner with internal teams and external advisors to assess prospective investments and support asset and contract valuations, contributing to analysis and reporting.
  • Data management & visualisation: Improve the collection, organisation, analysis, and visualisation of market data from sources such as AEMO, ASX Energy Futures, and SEC systems.

Who you are:
Experiences and Skills:

Must Have:

Your capabilities and areas of expertise that matter most for this role are:

  • Hands-on experience with PLEXOS, ideally including short-term schedule price forecasting;
  • Proficiency in programming languages to support data processing and workflow development, with preferences for Python, R and/or SQL;
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving and critical-thinking skills, with the ability to collaboratively interpret data and modelling outputs and produce and distribute meaningful insights across the organisation;
  • Numerical and computing skills to support the development of accessible analytical and reporting tools including Advanced Excel, PowerBI, and/or Tableau;

Highly Desirable:

  • Demonstrated knowledge and experience in the Australian energy market, particularly regarding the operation of wholesale markets, renewable energy assets, financial markets, and trading systems;
  • Tertiary qualifications (honours or advanced desirable) in Mathematics, Statistics, Engineering, Economics, Finance and/or another relevant specialisation;
  • An appreciation of Victorian Government policy targets, initiatives, and goals.

An empowered workforce
A career with SEC means you’ll be joining a new and vibrant ‘for purpose’ government-owned renewable energy company that:

  • Empowers you to influence how we accelerate Victoria’s renewable energy transition and decarbonise our economy.
  • Inspires you through meaningful, challenging work in an environment that encourages leadership and an entrepreneurial spirit.
  • Supports your growth through career advancement and professional development opportunities.
  • Provides hybrid work arrangements, with around 3 days working in Melbourne or Morwell, with flexible work options to meet individual circumstances, providing greater choice and autonomy.

How to Apply
We strongly encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people. We are also deeply committed to building an inclusive workplace that embraces diversity and people with disability, people from the LGBTIQ community, and people from culturally diverse backgrounds. SEC strives to create a respectful and collaborative workplace culture that allows all employees to thrive.

For further information and to explore this opportunity further please contact SECRecruitment@davidsonwp.com

Note: Applicants must be an Australian citizen, permanent resident or hold a valid work permit to be eligible to apply.

job.title: Group Manager Operations – Puffing Billy Railway
job.description:
• Lead rail service delivery, heritage, environmental and asset management functions
  • Executive leadership role at one of Victoria’s most iconic heritage attractions
  • Shape operational excellence, safety culture and long-term sustainability

Puffing Billy Railway is much more than a train ride – it transports visitors on a magical journey that becomes a cherished lifetime memory. As Australia’s foremost operating steam railway and one of the largest heritage railways in the world, Puffing Billy Railway is a Victorian State Government entity governed under the Puffing Billy Railway Act (2022) and reports to the Minister through the Department of Jobs, Skills, Industry and Regions.

Puffing Billy Railway is seeking an accomplished and forward-thinking Group Manager Operations to lead the organisation’s rail service delivery, heritage and environmental management, and asset management functions. Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer, this critical role ensures operational excellence, compliance, and the preservation of a unique cultural asset while strengthening the organisation’s future capability.

As Group Manager Operations, you will oversee rail service delivery, heritage, preservation, environmental and asset management strategies ensuring safe, reliable and compliant service delivery in line with relevant legislation including the Rail Safety National Law and the Puffing Billy Railway Act (2022). You will lead the development of data-driven operational strategies and foster a proactive culture of safety, continuous improvement, and regulatory compliance. You will also steward the organisation’s heritage, preservation and environmental programs, ensuring these vital custodial responsibilities are upheld and strengthened.

A key focus of the role is the development and maturation of the asset management accountability framework, ensuring alignment with Victorian Government requirements and long-term sustainability. You will guide and unify multidisciplinary teams, contribute to organisational strategic planning, and represent Puffing Billy Railway across government, industry and community forums. You will also lead cultural transformation, embed consistent business systems and processes, and mentor leaders to build capability across the organisation.

The ideal candidate will bring significant executive experience in operational leadership within complex, multi-stakeholder environments preferably in rail, transport, infrastructure, tourism, heritage or public sector contexts. You will demonstrate strong commercial and analytical skills, a track record in safety and risk management, and experience delivering operational and cultural transformation. Exceptional stakeholder engagement and communication skills are essential, as is a strong commitment to child safety, public sector values and community stewardship.

Gippsland Water provides essential water and wastewater services across the Gippsland region, supporting its customers, communities and the long-term prosperity of the region.   • Lead innovation initiatives, AI pilots and proofs of concept from opportunity identification through to scaled delivery and business-as-usual adoption.
  • Establish business cases and benefits realisation frameworks that demonstrate the value, productivity improvements and return on investment generated through AI and technology initiatives.

About You

You’re an experienced transformation, technology or data leader who knows how to turn emerging technologies into meaningful business outcomes. You can see the bigger picture, but you’re equally comfortable getting into the detail required to move ideas from strategy through to execution.

You’ll bring experience across AI, data governance and enterprise transformation, with the ability to establish practical frameworks, prioritise opportunities and manage the risks associated with emerging technology. You’ll be confident engaging with both technical and non-technical stakeholders, translating complexity into clear direction and building organisational capability along the way.

Must-Haves

  • Substantial experience across strategy, transformation, technology, innovation, business architecture, business improvement or organisational capability roles.
  • Demonstrated experience across AI and data governance, data quality and risk, ideally within a regulated or complex environment.
  • Strong experience across AI and data governance, data quality and risk, ideally within a regulated or complex environment.
  • Experience developing and implementing governance frameworks, policies, standards or operating models.

Nice-to-Have

Benefits & Why Gippsland Water

This is a unique opportunity to take on a highly influential leadership position at the intersection of AI, data, innovation and enterprise transformation, with genuine exposure to executive leadership, the Board and stakeholders across Gippsland Water.

Based in Traralgon, this is a permanent full-time position offering a flexible working model, a competitive salary package and additional benefits.
